{
  "participants": [
    {
      "login": "luke-jr",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "objected to altering -bind semantics for outbound traffic as it could break load balancing"
    },
    {
      "login": "frankomosh",
      "stance": "support",
      "note": "Concept ACK; suggested trial bind at startup and additional unit tests"
    },
    {
      "login": "gmaxwell",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "objected to overloading -bind because it breaks local LAN and VM bridge peer connections"
    },
    {
      "login": "vasild",
      "stance": "support",
      "note": "Concept ACK and Approach ACK; provided review feedback on validation, parsing, and tests"
    },
    {
      "login": "sedited",
      "stance": "neutral",
      "note": "asked whether the author was still working on rebasing and addressing open reviews"
    },
    {
      "login": "winterrdog",
      "stance": "support",
      "note": "Approach ACK, suggested alternative name -exitbind"
    }
  ],
  "claims": [
    {
      "id": "c:4216096603",
      "kind": "approach",
      "harm": "changing -bind semantics breaks setups that listen on one IP but load balance outbound connections",
      "quote": "This might break a scenario where someone wants to listen on one IP, but load balance outgoing connections. A new option might be better?",
      "blocking": false,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:4216582478",
        "c:4319952452",
        "c:4524241991"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "settled_by_id": "c:4524241991",
      "settled_by_quote": "Added `-outboundbind=<addr>` as a separate option instead of extending `-bind`"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3078339596",
      "kind": "safety",
      "harm": "storing the address without early validation silently kills outbound connections rather than failing loudly at startup",
      "quote": "misconfigured address fails loudly at init rather than silently killing outbound for that family",
      "blocking": false,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3793780005"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "settled_by_id": "rc:3793780005",
      "settled_by_quote": "Done. `IsAddrBindable()` does a trial `bind()` at init, so a misconfigured address fails startup."
    },
    {
      "id": "c:4317621161",
      "kind": "approach",
      "harm": "binding outbound connections via -bind prevents the node from connecting to peers on the local LAN or VM bridge interfaces",
      "quote": "as proposed here -bind=mypublicinterface would suddenly make my node unable to connect to stuff on my local lan (or, in VM on bridge interfaces)-- pretty surprising.",
      "blocking": true,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:4319952452",
        "c:4524241991"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "settled_by_id": "c:4524241991",
      "settled_by_quote": "Kept `-bind` semantics unchanged, so existing setups (including LAN/bridge peers) are unaffected"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3380992855",
      "kind": "interface",
      "harm": "allowing port numbers in -outboundbind causes confusion since outgoing source ports should not be specified",
      "quote": "this will allow ports to be included, e.g. `-outboundbind=1.2.4.5:5678` which better not be allowed to avoid confusion.",
      "blocking": false,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3793780883",
        "rc:3793781233"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "settled_by_id": "rc:3793781233",
      "settled_by_quote": "switched to `LookupHost()` so a port is rejected at startup."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3381134818",
      "kind": "interface",
      "harm": "silently swallowing unusable addresses masks configuration errors",
      "quote": "What's the reason to silently swallow such addresses? It would be more obvious if we return an error for those at startup, like we do for invalid values.",
      "blocking": false,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3793782102"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "settled_by_id": "rc:3793782102",
      "settled_by_quote": "Nothing is dropped silently."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3387250516",
      "kind": "interface",
      "harm": "first-wins prevents overriding earlier configuration settings",
      "quote": "Usually the notion is that the last one wins. E.g. `-outboundbind=1.2.3.4 -outboundbind=5.6.7.8` -- `5.6.7.8` should be used. This helps override earlier settings which might be out of one's control.",
      "blocking": false,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3793783043"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "settled_by_id": "rc:3793783043",
      "settled_by_quote": "first-wins matches the config-file convention (\"the first one is generally chosen\", doc/bitcoin-conf.md; reverse_precedence in common/settings.cpp)."
    }
  ],
  "support": [
    {
      "id": "r:4104595148",
      "verdict": "Concept ACK",
      "reason": "concept ACK.",
      "substantive": false
    },
    {
      "id": "r:4362316874",
      "verdict": "Concept ACK",
      "reason": "I agree that it is better to not change the semantic of the existent `-bind` and introduce a new option instead with a default value \"leave it to the OS\" which is the same as of before this PR.",
      "substantive": true
    },
    {
      "id": "r:4458989700",
      "verdict": "Approach ACK",
      "reason": "Approach ACK fa19b8c43489ffcc7693317af3c754992078e536",
      "substantive": false
    },
    {
      "id": "r:5187086729",
      "verdict": "Approach ACK",
      "reason": "approach ACK though, i might be TOO late for the name search party. i'd `-exitbind` in mind (inspired by TOR exit relays). will provide more review",
      "substantive": false
    }
  ],
  "notes": "Initial objections from luke-jr and gmaxwell against overloading -bind for outbound traffic were resolved by creating a dedicated -outboundbind option. Review feedback regarding trial binding, bare address parsing, and option precedence has been addressed and settled."
}

participants.note: objected to altering -bind semantics for outbound traffic as it could break load balancing

claims.harm: changing -bind semantics breaks setups that listen on one IP but load balance outbound connections
claims.quote: This might break a scenario where someone wants to listen on one IP, but load balance outgoing connections. A new option might be better?

claims.harm: storing the address without early validation silently kills outbound connections rather than failing loudly at startup
claims.quote: misconfigured address fails loudly at init rather than silently killing outbound for that family
claims.settled_by_quote: Done. `IsAddrBindable()` does a trial `bind()` at init, so a misconfigured address fails startup.

claims.harm: binding outbound connections via -bind prevents the node from connecting to peers on the local LAN or VM bridge interfaces
claims.quote: as proposed here -bind=mypublicinterface would suddenly make my node unable to connect to stuff on my local lan (or, in VM on bridge interfaces)-- pretty surprising.
claims.settled_by_quote: Kept `-bind` semantics unchanged, so existing setups (including LAN/bridge peers) are unaffected

claims.harm: allowing port numbers in -outboundbind causes confusion since outgoing source ports should not be specified
claims.quote: this will allow ports to be included, e.g. `-outboundbind=1.2.4.5:5678` which better not be allowed to avoid confusion.

claims.harm: silently swallowing unusable addresses masks configuration errors
claims.quote: What's the reason to silently swallow such addresses? It would be more obvious if we return an error for those at startup, like we do for invalid values.

claims.harm: first-wins prevents overriding earlier configuration settings
claims.quote: Usually the notion is that the last one wins. E.g. `-outboundbind=1.2.3.4 -outboundbind=5.6.7.8` -- `5.6.7.8` should be used. This helps override earlier settings which might be out of one's control.

support.reason: I agree that it is better to not change the semantic of the existent `-bind` and introduce a new option instead with a default value "leave it to the OS" which is the same as of before this PR.

changes: claim c:4317621161 added (resolved, blocking) by gmaxwell
